Ridhi set two sheets on the staffroom table: three years of cutoffs for Computer Science at the state college, and her own mock scores. “Sir, be honest. Is this branch realistic?”
Madhav Sir, the teacher who had coached earlier batches, ran a finger down the columns. “You've scored 118, 124 and 121. Last year's cutoff was around 145.”
“So it's a stretch?”
“A big one. But look here.” He tapped another row. “Information Technology at the same college, around 120. You're close to that.”
“So I could aim for both?”
“List both, keep working on your weak topics, and put the one you're likely to get where you can see it.”
Ridhi wrote two lines on a card. She had come in expecting a no, and left with a plan.

In January of Class 12, I was sure I'd get computer science at the top engineering college in our state. I'm Minakshi, and I'd never actually checked.

My friend Farida said, "Show your mocks to Mrs. Rao. She's coached students for fifteen years."

So I printed my last four mock scores and the college's closing ranks for the past three years. Mrs. Rao spread them out on the staffroom table and was quiet for a while.

"Computer science there is a stretch," she said. "Not impossible, but a stretch. Your mocks put you around here." She pointed. "But look: electronics and computer engineering at the same college closed here last year. That's realistic."

I felt disappointed for a minute. Then relieved. I had a real target instead of a wish. I kept computer science as my reach option and put the other branch right below it.

How did Minakshi feel on hearing the target branch was a stretch?
qa.a: Minakshi felt disappointed for a minute, then relieved to have a realistic target.

qa.q: What else could Minakshi ask Mrs. Rao?
qa.a: Minakshi could ask which topics would lift the mock scores most, to keep the reach option alive.

qa.q: How might Farida see the outcome of the advice?
qa.a: Farida likely feels glad and a bit proud, since the suggestion to see Mrs. Rao gave Minakshi a clear plan.

grounding: A reflective account of a student showing past cutoffs and mock scores to an experienced teacher and learning that the target branch is a stretch while a related one is achievable.

Physics teacher's note, entrance guidance hour

Sudha came to the guidance hour with her father, Samir, and a folder: her six mock scores and the last three years' closing ranks for civil engineering at the university she wanted. She asked me directly, "Is this realistic?"

I have coached students for this exam for many years, so I laid her scores beside past batches with similar marks. Most of them landed a few thousand ranks below her target. I told her plainly that the branch was a stretch. I also showed her that environmental engineering at the same university usually closed lower, and suited the interest in water systems she had mentioned.

Her father looked worried, but Sudha nodded and wrote both branches down in order. She said it felt better to know than to hope. I have given her two past papers a week to target her weakest topics.

qa.q: How many mock scores did Sudha bring?
How did Sudha seem to feel after hearing the branch was a stretch?
qa.a: She seemed steady and relieved, saying it felt better to know than to hope.

qa.q: What else could Sudha do to keep improving her chances?
qa.a: She could track her scores on the two weekly past papers and review progress with the teacher each month.

qa.q: How might Samir have felt during the conversation?
qa.a: Samir looked worried, perhaps anxious for his daughter, but likely reassured to see a realistic second option.
